items.stem: You need a single formula in the header cell that returns results for the whole column as new rows are added. Which approach fits best?

options.rationale: Correct: ARRAYFORMULA applies the calculation across the whole range and expands as data grows.
Manual fill does not auto-extend to new rows and clutters the sheet.
A pivot summarises data; it does not place a per-row calculation back in the column.
Conditional formatting changes appearance, not computed values.

items.explanation: Correct: ARRAYFORMULA applies the calculation across the whole range and expands as data grows.

items.stem: Which function reshapes and summarises a range using an SQL-like statement inside Google Sheets?

options.rationale: Correct: QUERY runs an SQL-like SELECT/GROUP BY against a range.
TRANSPOSE only swaps rows and columns.
SPARKLINE draws a tiny in-cell chart.
JOIN concatenates array values into a text string.

items.explanation: Correct: QUERY runs an SQL-like SELECT/GROUP BY against a range.

items.stem: Which TWO techniques reduce broken references when a model is copied or extended? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: absolute references keep the target fixed when copied.

options.text: Use named ranges for key inputs
options.rationale: Correct: named ranges stay valid and readable as the model grows.
Merging breaks many formulas and sorting.
Deleting data hides the problem rather than fixing the reference.

items.explanation: Correct: absolute references and named ranges both keep references stable as a model is copied or extended.
